sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Lake Derravaragh is an Irish mythological location. The lake lies in County Westmeath. It is also written Darravaraugh. It is a scenic body of water. On its shores Fionnuala and her brothers suffered a transformation. The brothers were the Children of Lir. Their evil stepmother Aífe worked the curse. Aífe turned the children into swans. The swans took to the lake and its waters. The transformation gave the lake its mythic fame. The Children of Lir became the swans of Derravaragh. The tale is among Ireland's best-known sorrow stories. The lake carries the memory of the curse. It stands as a mythological site in the Irish landscape. Aífe used her magic to bind the children. The swan form made the lake their home. The story places the site firmly in Irish myth.
objective: Present Lake Derravaragh as the mythological site of the Children of Lir's transformation.
